en: The Dyad on Roots to be Abandoned by Seeing, and the Triad on the Wholesome.

Dependent on a wholesome state with roots to be abandoned by vision (*dassanena pahātabba-hetuka*), an unwholesome state with roots not to be abandoned by vision (*nadassanena pahātabba-hetuka*) arises by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*). Under root [condition], one; ... pe ... under non-disappearance [condition], one.

Dependent on an unwholesome state with roots to be abandoned by vision, a state that is neither unwholesome nor wholesome with roots not to be abandoned by vision arises by way of root condition. ... Under root [condition], three; ... pe ... under non-disappearance [condition], three.
Dependent on an indeterminate state with roots not to be abandoned by vision, a state with roots not to be abandoned by vision... [arises].
A neutral state arises by way of the root condition... [Under] the root condition there are two; under the object condition, three ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition, three.
(In the section on the indeterminate, the count should be made for all conditions in this manner.)
